_comment: Model API capability catalog template, researched from official documentation as of 2026-11-09. Model keys match model_prices.json. The Myaaw runtime does NOT read this file yet; it does not automatically change requests, routing, tool handling, or thinking settings.

_schema.key_format: Exact provider model ID; all keys starting with _ are metadata, not models. Aliases and snapshots have fully expanded entries; alias_of/snapshot_of are informational, not inheritance mechanisms to execute.

value_semantics.true: Support is documented for this model on at least one endpoint/configuration described in notes. This does not guarantee support across all endpoints, regions, accounts, or feature combinations.
value_semantics.false: Explicitly unsupported according to the documentation checked, within the scope and limitations described in notes.
value_semantics.null: Unverified, specifications are unpublished, or documentation conflicts remain unresolved. Do not treat this as false or automatically enable the feature.
value_semantics.modality_arrays: Documented modalities; null means the list is unknown. An omitted modality does not automatically imply an explicit prohibition. Values: text/image/audio/video. PDF/documents are input formats, not additional modalities in this template.

fields.provider: openai | gemini | deepseek | anthropic; the provider's official API service, not a guarantee of support in the application's current adapter.
fields.status: active | preview | deprecated | unknown. Deprecated may indicate a legacy ID that still routes to an active model. Status does not guarantee availability for a particular account.
fields.input_modalities: Array of documented native input modalities, or null.
fields.output_modalities: Array of documented native output modalities, or null. Text metadata on image models does not necessarily mean free-form conversational text output; see notes. Audio transcription is distinguished from a text response modality.
fields.capabilities.thinking: Documented internal reasoning/thinking. This does not imply raw chain-of-thought exposure; summary/content settings differ by provider.
fields.capabilities.vision: Native image input understanding; not image generation, client-side OCR, or a guarantee of native video support.
fields.capabilities.function_calling: The model generates custom function/tool calls. This does not mean the model executes that code itself.
fields.capabilities.parallel_function_calling: Can generate multiple custom function calls in a single response; not merely multiple sequential tool steps.
fields.capabilities.structured_outputs: Schema-constrained final responses, not merely valid JSON or strict tool argument schemas.
fields.capabilities.json_mode: A valid JSON response mode without requiring a schema; not automatically inferred from structured_outputs or function_calling.
fields.capabilities.streaming: Incremental output on the relevant endpoint. SSE transport, bidirectional audio/video, and media generation differ; see endpoints/notes. Source conflicts are explicitly recorded.
fields.capabilities.prompt_caching: Input/prompt caching is supported; this does not guarantee cache hits, free caching, or support for both explicit and implicit caching.
fields.capabilities.batch_api: Support for the provider's Batch API, not client-side parallel requests.
fields.thinking.can_disable: An official control can fully disable thinking; minimal/low is not automatically equivalent to off.
fields.thinking.effort_values: Documented effort/level values for the model, not a universal scale across providers. null if only token budgets apply or specific values are unverified. API formats and conditions are described in thinking.notes.
fields.builtin_tools: Support for provider-executed/hosted tools: web_search, code_execution, file_search, image_generation, computer_use, url_context. Distinct from custom function calling and native output. code_execution includes Code Interpreter/hosted shell where documented. Anthropic web_fetch is mapped to url_context; Anthropic computer use is client-executed, so builtin_tools.computer_use is null and the availability is described in notes.
fields.limits: Exact integer token limits where published; null if unverified. context_window_tokens denotes a documented combined context window; max_input_tokens is not calculated by subtracting output from context. Do not add input/output limits without supporting evidence. Long decode and per-hop limits are explained in notes.
fields.endpoints: Array of normalized API family names, NOT literal HTTP routes. OpenAI/DeepSeek: chat_completions, responses, batch, realtime, assistants, fine_tuning, image_generation, image_edit, anthropic_messages. Gemini: generate_content, stream_generate_content, batch_generate_content, interactions, live. Anthropic: messages, message_batches. null if unverified. Consult official sources for actual endpoints/SDK methods; not every feature is available in every API family.
fields.sources: Official documentation URLs checked. Failed requests/404 responses are recorded in notes; those URLs do not constitute evidence of feature support.
fields.notes: Endpoint limitations, status, source conflicts, request controls, and feature conditions. Read before using capability flags to construct requests.

_research_notes: Scope: 124 exact IDs from model_prices.json, including aliases and snapshots; not 124 distinct architectures/models. Prices are not used as evidence of model capabilities.

Research uses public documentation, not paid inference tests or authenticated models.list requests. Some restricted/private models have no public cards; their flags remain null rather than being guessed from family names.

Snapshots use canonical profiles only when the snapshots are officially documented. Where separate specifications are unavailable, inheritance limitations are explained in notes. Latest aliases can change and must be researched again.

Individually supported features are not necessarily compatible in combination, such as tools + thinking + forced tool choice or structured outputs + built-in tools. A true flag means at least one supported configuration exists; configuration restrictions still apply.
This file catalogs provider capabilities, not Myaaw adapter capabilities. The current runtime uses its own provider logic; this update adds no loader or runtime code changes.
Models outside the price catalog, such as embeddings, moderation, media-only models without text output prices, and managed agents, are not added to this catalog.

Anthropic coverage lists models that remain callable on the first-party Claude API. Retired models, including Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Opus 4, and Claude Sonnet 4, are excluded even where historical price tables still show them. Claude Sonnet 4.5 is included as deprecated because it remains callable until 2026-11-30.

Anthropic's provider-hosted web_search, web_fetch, and code_execution tools are represented in builtin_tools; web_fetch is explicitly mapped to the generic url_context field. Anthropic computer use, browser use, bash, and text editor are client-executed tools, so they are described in notes rather than marked as provider-hosted builtins.

thinking.notes: Thinking defaults to enabled/high. Chat Completions and Anthropic expose thinking.type=enabled|disabled; Responses uses reasoning.effort, where none disables thinking. Chat Completions also documents reasoning_effort=none|low|high|max; an explicit thinking.type takes precedence. Compatibility synonyms are mapped, not distinct effort levels. reasoning_content is returned by Chat Completions; Responses exposes reasoning_text rather than reasoning summaries.

notes: Official public documentation checked 2026-11-09. deepseek-flash is currently served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. The version name is not substituted for the documented API model ID.

The feature table advertises a 1M context, but does not give an exact integer in the fetched specifications; context_window_tokens and max_input_tokens remain null rather than assuming decimal or binary units. Chat Completions explicitly defines 384K output as 393216 tokens; input plus generated tokens must fit the context. Output includes reasoning and final-answer tokens.

Parallel function calling is explicitly always enabled in Responses; parallel_tool_calls is ignored. Support does not imply that the caller can disable parallel calls or that every API format exposes the same control.

JSON mode guarantees JSON syntax, not adherence to an arbitrary response schema. Chat Completions enumerates text/json_object only. Responses says text.format is fully supported without enumerating schema constraints in that guide, so structured_outputs remains null. Beta strict=true function argument schemas are supported in both thinking modes, but are not equated to schema-constrained final responses.

When tools are present in Chat Completions, preserve all prior reasoning_content in subsequent assistant messages, including turns without a tool call. Missing reasoning_content can cause HTTP 400. Forced required/named tool_choice is unsupported while thinking is enabled; disable thinking to use it.
Prompt caching is automatic and best-effort. No public Batch API support was established; batch_api=null is not a claim of unsupported batch processing.

Native image input is documented for Flash via Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic APIs. Accepted formats are JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP. No native audio or video input/output is established. The modality arrays list documented support only.

Responses ignores web_search for Flash, and ignores file_search/code_interpreter/computer_use and other unsupported built-in tools. External client functions remain available and can implement these tasks. Standalone Search/Fetch APIs and harness integrations are not counted as native model tools or a distinct URL-context feature.
